title: Nano-Nb Superconducting 3D Josephson Junctions Arrays in Cu-Normal Matrix: Superconducting Phase Coherence and Quantum Fluctuations Properties
authors: R. L. de Almeida, J. Albino Aguiar, J. A. H. Coaquira
abstract: To address the complex interplay of microstructural evolution, phase separation, superconductivity coherence and quantum fluctuations, we prepared Cuxwt%Nb series of granular samples by rapidly cooling, where the niobium concentration varied (x = 3, 5, 15, 20). By employing this method, we successfully obtained samples characterized by well-defined precipitates of niobium, featuring regular sizes and grain spacing. The goal was to establish a systematic and robust method approach for obtaining samples with different of sub-micrometric precipitates distributions but also to investigate their superconducting properties. Structural characterization by optical and Scanning Electron Microscopy, dc Mdc[H,T] ac inductive , as well the magneto-transport measures rhodc[H,T], Rdc[V,I.H,T], I[V,H,T] and [H,T,I] were done. Also, using a micro Hall sensor with 10 measuring transverse voltage bridges regularly distributed, we were able to obtain the real external applied magnetic field value inside of the chamber sample space. Thus e studied the dependence of configuration of the Nb grains in the superconducting coupling order parameter properties that connects the grains superconductors to the normal Cu matrix. We verify through magnetization and transport measures the signature of the double transition. This, when we apply current of different intensities, in the transport measures, and different field values, in the inductive measures. This behavior is an indication that our system is made up of by a collection of superconducting grains immersed in a well-organized in a non-superconducting matrix. The results indicate that the superconducting properties of these systems are manifested usually through two transition temperatures Tc(H) e TcJ(H).
summary: This work investigates superconducting properties in granular $	ext{Cu-Nb}$ alloys, treating them as arrays of Josephson junctions embedded in a normal metal. By measuring transport and magnetic responses, the authors confirm the existence of two distinct superconducting transitions, attributing one to the bulk grains and the other to the weak coupling between them. The results provide quantitative parameters for the Josephson coupling and evidence of quantum interference effects.
main_problem: To investigate the complex interplay between microstructural evolution, phase separation, superconducting phase coherence, and quantum fluctuations in granular superconducting systems.
main_result: The system exhibits a clear signature of a double superconducting transition ($T_c(H)$ and $T_{cJ}(H)$), confirming it is composed of superconducting grains weakly coupled within a normal matrix.
method: The study combines advanced structural characterization (SEM) with comprehensive magnetotransport and magnetic susceptibility measurements (MPMS/PPMS).
model_or_system: The physical system is a Cu-Nb granular superconductor ($	ext{Cu}_x	ext{wt\%Nb}$), where superconducting Nb precipitates are embedded in a normal Cu matrix. The behavior is modeled using effective medium-field theory.
key_observables: Two distinct transition temperatures ($T_c(H)$ and $T_{cJ}(H)$), double transition signatures in magnetization/transport, and quantum interference oscillations in critical current ($I_c$).
important_parameters: Critical fields ($H_{c1J} \approx 100 	ext{ Oe}$, $H_{c2J} \approx 200 	ext{ Oe}$), and an oscillation period of $H_{	ext{perio}} \approx 24 	ext{ Oe}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be modeled as a collection of superconducting grains immersed in a non-superconducting matrix, and that the grain spacing is regular.
figures_summary: Figures show microstructures revealing Nb precipitates and plots illustrate the field-dependent critical current ($I_c$) exhibiting small oscillations modulated by the external field.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing a systematic method for sample preparation (rapid cooling) to detailed structural characterization, followed by comprehensive magnetotransport and magnetic susceptibility measurements to diagnose the superconducting coupling mechanisms.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence of quantum interference effects (oscillations) in a mesoscopic superconducting network, which is relevant to understanding phase coherence and quantum fluctuations in disordered superconducting systems.
